paragraphs.title: Jonathan Launches an Attack and Seeks a Sign

easy.explanation: Jonathan went with the young man who bore his armor.
easy.q: Who went with Jonathan toward the Philistine garrison?

easy.explanation: The verse says Jonathan told not his father.
easy.q: Whom did Jonathan not tell about his departure?

answers: The Lord can save only through many
The Lord cannot save in battle
The Lord can save by many or by few
easy.explanation: Jonathan said there was no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.
easy.q: What did Jonathan believe about the Lord's power to save?

answers: To know whether to go up to them
medium.explanation: Their response would show Jonathan whether the Lord had delivered them into Israel's hand.
medium.q: Why did Jonathan use the Philistines' response as a sign?

answers: Tarry until we come to you
medium.explanation: If they told Jonathan to tarry until they came to him, he would not go up.
medium.q: What response would cause Jonathan to remain where he was?

answers: A man who carries a warrior's weapons
A man who rules the camp
A man who guards the garrison
medium.explanation: Jonathan's armor-bearer carried and used weapons alongside him.
medium.q: What is an armor-bearer in this passage?

answers: He acted secretly and on his own initiative
He was afraid of his armor-bearer
He had already won the battle
challenge.explanation: Jonathan went secretly, without informing his father.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jonathan's leaving without telling Saul?

answers: His faith gave him courage, while the sign directed his next step
The sign proved that he had no faith
challenge.explanation: Jonathan trusted the Lord's power but sought guidance for the immediate action.
challenge.q: How are Jonathan's faith and his request for a sign related?

answers: One meant they should go up, and the other meant they should wait
Both meant they should go up
challenge.explanation: “Come up unto us” was the sign to go up, while “Tarry until we come” meant to stay.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the two responses Jonathan proposed?

paragraphs.title: The Attack on the Philistine Outpost

answers: Hebrews coming forth out of the holes
easy.explanation: The Philistines said, “Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes.”
easy.q: What did the Philistines call Jonathan and his armor-bearer?

easy.explanation: Jonathan said, “Come up after me.”
easy.q: What did Jonathan tell his armor-bearer after the Philistines spoke?

easy.explanation: The first slaughter was about twenty men.
easy.q: About how many men fell in the first slaughter?

answers: Jonathan climbed on his hands and feet
They waited for the soldiers to come down
medium.explanation: Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer after him.
medium.q: How did Jonathan and his armor-bearer reach the garrison?

answers: Trembling and confusion spread through the Philistine camp
medium.explanation: The attack caused trembling in the host and a great shaking of the earth.
medium.q: What was the result of their small attack?

answers: He killed men after Jonathan struck them
medium.explanation: The armor-bearer continued killing Philistines after Jonathan's attack.
medium.q: What does “his armourbearer slew after him” mean?

answers: It caused fear, confusion, and an earthquake
The entire camp had already surrendered
Saul immediately sent a large army
challenge.explanation: The passage describes trembling in the host, the field, and among the people, along with an earthquake.
challenge.q: Why did the attack of two men affect the whole camp?

answers: He understood the invitation to come up as permission to attack
He asked Saul for another sign
challenge.explanation: When the Philistines said, “Come up to us,” Jonathan acted.
challenge.q: What does Jonathan's action show about the sign he received?

answers: It was the beginning of the fear that spread through the camp
It happened after the camp had already fled
It had no connection to the confusion
challenge.explanation: The trembling and confusion followed Jonathan and his armor-bearer's attack.
challenge.q: How did the first slaughter relate to the confusion in the camp?

paragraphs.title: Confusion in the Philistine Camp and Israel's Advance

easy.explanation: The watchmen saw that the multitude melted away.
easy.q: What did Saul's watchmen see in the Philistine camp?

easy.explanation: A count showed that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
easy.q: Who was missing from Saul's camp?

answers: Every man's sword was against his fellow
They were hidden in the hills
easy.explanation: The Philistines fought one another in the confusion.
easy.q: What happened to the Philistines' swords?

medium.explanation: Saul wanted to know who had gone from the camp.
medium.q: Why did Saul ask the people to be numbered?

answers: Hebrews who had been with the Philistines and Israelites who had hidden
medium.explanation: The Hebrews turned to Israel, and the hidden Israelites followed after the fleeing Philistines.
medium.q: Who joined Israel's pursuit of the Philistines?

answers: The Philistine force scattered and weakened
The force gathered and grew stronger
medium.explanation: “Melted away” describes the Philistines' dispersal and defeat.
medium.q: What does “the multitude melted away” mean?

answers: The Philistines' flight gave the Hebrews and hidden Israelites opportunity to join
It caused Israel to hide more deeply
challenge.explanation: As the Philistines fled, both groups joined Saul and Jonathan in battle.
challenge.q: How did the confusion help more people join Israel?

answers: He sought guidance but hurried when the battle grew louder
challenge.explanation: Saul began to seek God's direction but stopped the priest as the Philistine confusion increased.
challenge.q: What is suggested by Saul first calling for the ark and then telling the priest to withdraw his hand?

answers: The Lord saved Israel that day
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes, “So the Lord saved Israel that day.”
challenge.q: What was the overall result by verse 23?

paragraphs.title: The Oath Not to Eat and the Honey

easy.explanation: Saul cursed the man that ate any food until evening.
easy.q: What did Saul forbid the people to eat until evening?

easy.explanation: There was honey upon the ground.
easy.q: What did the people find in the wood?

easy.explanation: Jonathan dipped the end of his rod in the honeycomb and tasted it.
easy.q: Who tasted the honey?

answers: They immediately stopped pursuing the Philistines
medium.explanation: The people were faint because they had not eaten.
medium.q: What effect did Saul's oath have on the soldiers?

answers: He did not hear when Saul charged the people
medium.explanation: Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath.
medium.q: Why did Jonathan not know about the oath?

medium.explanation: The people had become weak from hunger and exertion.
medium.q: What does “the people were faint” mean here?

answers: The oath weakened the people and reduced the victory
The people had eaten too much
challenge.explanation: Jonathan said the people would have made a greater slaughter if they had eaten freely.
challenge.q: Why did Jonathan criticize Saul's command?

answers: He was weary, and the honey refreshed him
He wanted to reject God's law
He had not taken part in the pursuit
challenge.explanation: After tasting the honey, his eyes were enlightened.
challenge.q: What does the honey reveal about Jonathan's condition?

answers: Maintaining the pursuit versus giving the soldiers food and strength
Jonathan and his armor-bearer dividing the spoil
Saul and the priest choosing a camp
challenge.explanation: Saul's oath was meant to preserve the pursuit but instead weakened the army.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Eating with the Blood and Correcting the Sin

answers: They ate the meat with the blood
They returned it to the Philistines
easy.explanation: The people slew the animals and ate them with the blood.
easy.q: What did the people do when they reached the spoil?

easy.explanation: Saul commanded the people to roll a great stone to him.
easy.q: What did Saul use to correct the manner of eating?

easy.explanation: Saul built an altar unto the Lord.
easy.q: What did Saul build unto the Lord?

answers: The people ate the meat without properly draining its blood
medium.explanation: The people ate the animals with the blood still in them.
medium.q: Why was eating with the blood considered a sin?

answers: By killing the animals properly on the stone before eating
medium.explanation: Saul told them to bring the animals and slay them there before eating.
medium.q: How could the people eat without sinning?

answers: Bring or move a large stone to Saul
medium.explanation: Saul ordered the people to bring a great stone to him.
medium.q: What does “roll a great stone unto me” mean?

answers: Both were part of restoring proper obedience to the Lord
The altar was built to hide the spoil
challenge.explanation: Saul first corrected the people's eating and then built an altar unto the Lord.
challenge.q: How were the stone and the altar related to correcting the people's sin?

answers: To learn whether to continue pursuing the Philistines
To discover who had eaten honey
challenge.explanation: Saul asked whether he should go down after the Philistines.
challenge.q: Why did Saul seek counsel from God afterward?

answers: Some sin or obstacle needed to be investigated
challenge.explanation: Saul recognized that the lack of an answer required him to find the cause.
challenge.q: What can be inferred because God did not answer Saul that day?

paragraphs.title: The Lot, Jonathan's Guilt, and His Rescue

easy.explanation: The lot was cast between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken.
easy.q: Upon whom did the lot finally fall?

easy.explanation: Jonathan said he had tasted a little honey.
easy.q: What had Jonathan tasted?

easy.explanation: Saul declared, “Thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.”
easy.q: What did Saul say should happen to Jonathan?

medium.explanation: Saul used a perfect lot to identify the guilty person.
medium.q: How was the guilty person identified?

answers: He had wrought a great salvation in Israel
He had not fought in the battle
medium.explanation: The people said Jonathan had wrought a great salvation in Israel.
medium.q: Why did the people oppose Jonathan's death?

answers: They prevented him from being put to death
They delivered him to the Philistines
They sent him to pursue the enemy
medium.explanation: The people protected Jonathan so that he died not.
medium.q: What does “the people rescued Jonathan” mean?

answers: Saul demanded Jonathan's death, while the people demanded his rescue
Saul wanted to rescue Jonathan, while the people wanted him dead
Both wanted the pursuit to end
challenge.explanation: Saul said Jonathan should die, but the people rescued him.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Saul's decision and the people's response?

answers: As a great salvation in Israel
As the cause of Israel's defeat
challenge.explanation: They credited Jonathan with a great salvation in Israel.
challenge.q: How did the people describe Jonathan's contribution?

answers: It did not immediately identify Jonathan alone as guilty
It showed that the people refused the investigation
challenge.explanation: Saul and Jonathan were first taken together, and only afterward was Jonathan taken by himself.
challenge.q: What is significant about the lot first taking Saul and Jonathan together?

paragraphs.title: Saul's Wars and Consolidation of the Kingdom

answers: He gave it to the Philistines
easy.explanation: The verse says Saul took the kingdom over Israel.
easy.q: What did Saul do concerning the kingdom of Israel?

easy.explanation: Saul smote the Amalekites and delivered Israel from its spoilers.
easy.q: Which people did Saul defeat and save Israel from?

answers: Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, and the Philistines
easy.explanation: The passage names Moab, Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines.
easy.q: Which enemies are listed in these verses?

answers: His victories strengthened his rule and defended Israel
The wars caused him to leave the throne
medium.explanation: The account of his battles follows the statement that he took the kingdom over Israel.
medium.q: How did Saul's wars relate to his kingdom?

answers: They were surrounding or threatening enemies of Israel
They were all members of Saul's family
medium.explanation: They are presented as enemies against whom Saul fought.
medium.q: What do the listed enemies have in common?

answers: He acted successfully and forcefully in war
medium.explanation: The wording describes Saul's military success against Israel's enemies.
medium.q: What does “he did valiantly” or “he smote” convey about Saul's actions?

answers: Saul faced threats from several directions and strengthened his power
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes the wide range of Saul's military campaigns.
challenge.q: What does the move from one enemy to a broad list of enemies suggest?

answers: Wherever Saul went against them, he defeated or troubled his enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes Saul's success wherever he engaged his enemies.
challenge.q: What does “whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them” mean?

answers: He is shown protecting Israel from its plunderers
He is shown handing Israel over to Amalek
It has no connection to his kingship
challenge.explanation: The verse highlights Saul's deliverance of Israel from those who spoiled it.
challenge.q: How does Saul's victory over Amalek relate to his role as king?

easy.explanation: Jonathan is listed among Saul's sons.
easy.q: Which of these was one of Saul's sons?

easy.explanation: The younger daughter was named Michal.
easy.q: What was the name of Saul's younger daughter?

easy.explanation: Abner, the son of Ner, was captain of Saul's host.
easy.q: Who was the captain of Saul's host?

answers: His daughters, wife, army captain, and relatives
medium.explanation: The passage gives details about Saul's family, relatives, and military leadership.
medium.q: What do these verses list besides Saul's sons?

answers: He sent them to the Philistines
He scattered them among other nations
medium.explanation: Saul gathered capable men to himself.
medium.q: What did Saul do when he saw strong or valiant men?

answers: A capable and courageous military man
A child who could not fight
A farmer working in the field
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to men suitable for military service.
medium.q: What does “a strong man, or any valiant man” mean in context?

answers: Saul needed a strong, organized army over time
challenge.explanation: The war continued throughout Saul's reign, so he gathered capable warriors.
challenge.q: What does the continuing war and gathering of valiant men suggest?

answers: To present the royal household and the leadership surrounding Saul
To explain the oath concerning honey
challenge.explanation: The list introduces Saul's family and the principal figures around his rule.
challenge.q: Why are family members and the army commander mentioned together?

answers: The conflict continued throughout Saul's reign
The war lasted only one day
The Philistines ceased to be enemies
challenge.explanation: The verse says there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul.
challenge.q: What does “all the days of Saul” show about the conflict with the Philistines?
